invariants: Tx is created ONLY by PgSession::in_tx (the constructor is pub(crate)) and is valid only inside that closure; its methods block on the runtime handle and would panic if called from async context.
Tx never issues BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK or set_config: in_tx opens the transaction and sets the owner config before the closure runs; dropping the transaction uncommitted rolls back.
Errors from tokio-postgres map through the From<tokio_postgres::Error> impl in error.rs (the ? operator) - never map them by hand.
The Transaction and the Handle stay in private fields; no tokio or tokio-postgres type appears in a public signature (params use &(dyn ToSql + Sync), exactly as PgSession's call_* do).
This module has NO #[cfg(test)] module: it contains no pure logic, and unit tests must never touch a live database.

Two lifetimes, never one: Tx<'t, 'c> borrows the Transaction for 't while the Transaction itself borrows the Client for 'c. Collapsing them into a single lifetime makes the borrow outlive the closure scope and in_tx cannot commit (E0505/E0597 - hit and fixed during the build).
responsibilities: Hold the one open transaction plus the runtime handle for the duration of one PgSession::in_tx closure; all fields private.

Offer the same five call_* helpers as PgSession (call_scalar, call_void, call_json, call_bool, call_text) with identical signatures and row semantics, executed on the open transaction instead of a fresh one.
Map the optional row exactly as PgSession does: call_scalar returns row.get(0); call_bool unwraps to false when there is no row.
summary: The handle for one open owner-scoped transaction: PgSession's call_* surface, bound to the single transaction PgSession::in_tx opened.
